import html # Example HTML template with a placeholder for user content. html_template = """ User Page
{user_content}
""" def construct_html_response(content: str) -> str: """ Injects user-supplied content into an HTML template after escaping it. Parameters ---------- content : str The raw text supplied by the user. This may contain characters that need to be escaped to avoid breaking the HTML structure or executing unwanted scripts. Returns ------- str The final HTML string with the escaped user content inserted into ``html_template``. The placeholder `{user_content}` is replaced by the sanitized value. Notes ----- - Uses :func:`html.escape` to neutralize characters such as `<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, and `'`. This mitigates injection attacks (XSS) by ensuring that the user content cannot terminate tags or introduce new ones. - The function does not raise any custom exceptions; any errors arising from malformed input will propagate as standard Python errors. """ # Ensure the content is a string and escape special HTML characters. escaped_content = html.escape(str(content), quote=True) # Safely format the template, replacing the placeholder with escaped content. return html_template.format(user_content=escaped_content)
